newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile authorizes big Los Pelambres investment.
newsitem.headline: Chile authorizes big Los Pelambres investment.

text.p: Chile has authorized a $2.75 billion investment in Los Pelambres copper mine by British company Los Pelambres Investment Co Ltd and Dutch-registered firms Nippon LP Resources BV and MM LP Holding BV, said the government's Foreign Investment Committee.
The authorization makes Los Pelambres the second largest investment ever approved by the committee, after the Collahuasi copper mine.

The authorized investment is much higher than the $1.3 billion the mine's owners plan to spend on the project, giving them leeway to bring extra capital for the scheme into Chile without having to seek further permission from the government.
Los Pelambres Investment Company Ltd, controlled by Chile's Luksic group through London-quoted Antofagasta Holdings plc, owns 60 percent of the mine which is in the Fourth Region.
Antofagasta Holdings announced in May that it had agreed to sell a 40 percent stake in the mine to two Japanese groups for $256 million.
